standards: apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace;

use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution;

select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems;
communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate;
create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas;
analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas; and
display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.
calculate rise and run such as the rise and run of stair stringers or roof pitch;
distinguish the purpose and difference of a linear and non-linear increase and decrease of a variable with time such as cost or profit;
write systems of equations and inequalities from real-life situations that compare "best deal opportunities" with profit and expenses in businesses;
use linear programing to maximize or minimize linear objective function in real-life situations and determine the reasonableness of solutions;
express numbers as powers of 10 in business and industry settings;
determine the powers and roots of numbers;
apply compound interest formulas related to operating a business; and
use exponential decay models to determine the depreciation on equipment used in business and industry and explain the meaning of models.
identify various geometric figures in order to identify what formulas are needed to solve situational problems;
compute measurements such as area, surface area, volume, perimeter, and circumference in order to prepare engineering drawings for projects;
use trigonometric functions such as sine, cosine, tangent, cotangent, cosecant, and secant to calculate angles and length of sides;
apply Heron's formula for finding areas of triangles when the height is not known;
determine how changing dimensions will affect the perimeter, area, surface area, or volume in a project;
determine how angles will affect structural strength and stability;
apply right triangle relationships using the Pythagorean Theorem, special right triangles, and trigonometry for roof construction, building the frame of a car, or calculating machined parts;
determine the materials needed for a job or project by finding missing parts of a circle;
draw orthographic and isometric views and use them to produce engineering drawings;
use cross-sections, including conic sections, of three-dimensional figures to relate to plane figures in specific detail on an engineered drawing; and
explain and use auxiliary views, revolutions, intersections, and engineered drawings.
use dimensional analysis to select an appropriate tool to make measurements;
apply accurate readings of both U.S. customary and metric measuring devices to a problem situation;
square, measure, and cut materials to specified dimensions;
draw segments to scale using an accurate scale and measure segments that are drawn to scales;
convert temperature values between Celsius and Fahrenheit in situations involving thermodynamics; and
determine length, distance, area, surface area, volume, and weight with appropriate unit labels.
use rates and linear functions to solve problems involving finance and budgeting, including compensations and deductions;
solve problems related to local, state, and federal taxes;
analyze data to make decisions about banking and finance;
use mathematical processes with algebraic formulas, numerical techniques, and graphs to solve problems related to job cost analysis;
identify what parameters to change such as cost of materials, cost of labor, and work time required to improve the overall cost of a project; and
identify the most reasonable mathematical solution using estimation.
interpret and present situations in terms of given graphs and that fit graphics;
apply Ohm's Law and Kirchhoff's laws to troubleshoot electrical circuits;
collect and organize data; make and interpret scatterplots; and model, predict, and make decisions and critical judgments; and
prepare technical reports and presentations with visual media or models, including tables, graphs, and verbal descriptions.
identify the line types used on engineering drawings;
identify selected symbols commonly used on engineering drawings;
identify the components of engineering drawings;
read, interpret, and create engineering drawings; and
use proper nomenclature when identifying engineering or manufacturing processes.
explain the importance of dressing appropriately, speaking politely, and conducting oneself in a manner appropriate for the profession and work site;
describe teamwork, group dynamics, and conflict resolution and how they can impact the collective outcome;
present written and oral technical communication in a clear, concise, and effective manner for a variety of purposes and audiences;
identify time-management skills such as prioritizing tasks, following schedules, and tending to goal-relevant activities and how these practices optimize efficiency and results;
define work ethic and discuss the characteristics of a positive work ethic, including punctuality, dependability, reliability, and responsibility for reporting for duty and performing assigned tasks;
demonstrate respect for differences in the workplace;
identify the importance and benefits of meritocracy, a hard work ethic, and equal opportunity in the workplace;
identify consequences relating to discrimination and harassment;
demonstrate knowledge of personal and occupational health and safety practices, including first aid, in the workplace;
describe the roles and responsibilities of managers;
identify career development and entrepreneurship opportunities in the field;
identify appropriate training, education, or certification in the field; and
identify legal and ethical responsibilities in relation to the field.
demonstrate dressing appropriately, speaking politely, and conducting oneself in a manner appropriate for the profession and work site;
analyze how teams can produce better outcomes through cooperation, contribution, and collaboration from members of the team;
present written and oral technical communication in a clear, concise, and effective manner for a variety of purposes and audiences, including explaining and justifying decisions;
use time-management skills independently and in groups to prioritize tasks, follow schedules, and tend to goal-relevant activities in a way that optimizes efficiency and results;
describe the importance of and demonstrate punctuality, dependability, reliability, and responsibility in reporting for duty and performing assigned tasks as directed;
demonstrate respect for differences in the workplace;
identify the importance and benefits of meritocracy, a hard work ethic, and equal opportunity in the workplace;
identify consequences relating to discrimination and harassment;

demonstrate knowledge of personal and occupational health and safety, applicable regulations, and first aid in the workplace and discuss why it is critical for employees and employers to maintain a safe work environment;
compare skills and characteristics of managers and leaders in the workplace; and
identify career development opportunities in the field: (i) education and training; (ii) credentialing; (iii) internships and apprenticeships; and (iv) entrepreneurship opportunities; and
demonstrate an understanding of legal and ethical responsibilities in relation to the field.
describe the impact of internships, career development, and entrepreneurship opportunities in occupational safety and compliance;
identify and analyze career advancement opportunities in occupational safety and compliance at various levels in an organization such as employee, supervisor, and manager; and

identify and explain requirements to obtain professional credentials such as a Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Construction Health and Safety Technician (CHST), Occupational Hygiene and Safety Technician (OHST), Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM), Certified Environmental Manager (CEM), and Board of Certified Safety Professionals (BCSP) in the fields of occupational safety and health compliance.
explain and discuss responsibilities of workers and employers to promote safety and health in the workplace;
explain the OSHA general duty clause and the rights of workers to a safe and healthy workplace;
explain and discuss the importance of OSHA standards and requirements for organizations;

explain the role of industrial hygiene in occupational health and safety and describe various types of industrial hygiene hazards, including physical, chemical, airborne, excessive noise, physiological, biological, and ergonomic hazards;
identify types and explain appropriate use of personal protective equipment (PPE) used in industry;
explain the importance of safe walking and working surfaces in the workplace and identify best practices for preventing or reducing slips, trips, and falls in the workplace;
describe types of electrical hazards in the workplace and risks associated with these hazards;
describe control methods to prevent electrical hazards in the workplace;
analyze hazards of handling, storing, using, and transporting hazardous materials;
identify and discuss ways to reduce exposure to hazardous materials in the workplace;
identify workplace health and safety resources, including emergency plans and Safety Data Sheets (SDS);
discuss how emergency plans and SDS are used to make decisions in the workplace;
describe elements of a safety and health program, including management leadership, worker participation, and training;
explain the purpose and importance of written emergency action and fire protection plans;
describe key components of written emergency action and fire protection plans such as evacuation plans and emergency exit routes, list of fire hazards, and identification of emergency personnel;
explain components of a hazard communication program; and

explain and give examples of safety and health training requirements specified by standard setting organizations such as American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists (ACGIH), American National Standard Institute (ANSI), National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), and Board of Certified Safety Professionals (BCSP).
identify the objectives of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA);
identify the objectives of the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ);
describe how the EPA and the TCEQ monitor compliance and enforce regulations; and

identify and describe federal environmental acts, including Endangered Species Act (ESA); Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA); Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA); Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA); Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (CERCLA or Superfund); and Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA).
explain the significance of periodic and effective inspections for hazard control;
describe the processes for reporting a hazard or accident to an immediate supervisor;
explain the value of training programs that promote awareness of safety policies and procedures in the workplace;
select appropriate PPE such as safety glasses, face shields, aprons, and gloves based on workplace requirements;
summarize the purpose of protecting the body, including eyes, face, head, feet, arms, hands, ears, and torso, from industrial hazards;
identify and describe specific causes of an incident;
explain the necessity of a comprehensive safety program;
outline principles of housekeeping, including order and cleanliness; and
describe how a disorganized workplace, litter, and debris can create unsafe conditions that lead to accidents and illness in the workplace.
identify and describe potential types of workplace security events;
identify and describe strategies to enhance workplace security; and
identify and describe strategies to prevent workplace violence.
explain how the science of ergonomics is used in various industries such as manufacturing, construction, medical, and energy;

evaluate workplace tasks to identify potential ergonomic problems related to body positions, including posture and awkward positions, and body movements, including repetitive movement, applying extreme force, reaching, pushing, pulling, bending, and weightlifting;
describe primary body systems impacted by ergonomics; and
evaluate workplace conditions that can produce physical fatigue.
explain the role of industrial hygiene in occupational safety;
describe the process to identify hazards using various methods, including reviewing chemical inventories and evaluating potential hazards associated with chemicals found in the workplace;
identify and describe various categories of industrial hygiene hazards;
compare various types of workplace hazards, including biological, chemical, ergonomic, and physical;
identify categories of hazardous substances and describe short- and long-term health effects resulting from exposure to each hazardous substance;
explain industrial hygiene and occupational exposures concepts, including acute and chronic exposures; and
describe essential responsibilities of supervisors, managers, and safety personnel in the prevention of occupational hazards.
describe the Occupational Safety Health Administration (OSHA) Hazard Communication Standard, including standards for hazard classification;
interpret and analyze SDS and container labeling requirements;
explain the purpose and importance of proper chemical storage;
describe physical properties of hazardous materials;
identify and describe ways in which hazardous materials enter the body;
explain various strategies to protect from inhalation of harmful airborne substances; and
discuss the significance of safety precautions when handling and using compressed gas in the workplace.
identify and describe steps to reduce noise exposure;
explain the noise reduction rating (NRR) developed by the EPA;
explain the purpose and importance of eye washes and emergency showers in the workplace;
identify and describe possible hazards related to heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems;
identify and describe possible hazards related to indoor air quality, including ventilation and adequate air flow;
identify steps to reduce hazards related to general machine guarding, power hand tools, and tool safety;
identify and describe motor vehicle safety and security management techniques such as accident prevention strategies, driver training programs, and vehicle inspection protocols;
describe steps to reduce hazards related to powered industrial trucks; and
identify and describe possible hazards related to ladders and scaffolds.
identify and describe proper storage techniques for flammable or combustible materials;
identify and describe the importance of fire systems inspections, fire confinement, emergency exits, and emergency lighting;
describe the importance and maintenance of portable fire extinguishers;
differentiate between fire and combustion; and
describe classes of fire controlled by various extinguishing agents.
describe characteristics of fixed wet and dry chemical extinguishing systems;
describe physical characteristics of carbon dioxide, halogenated hydrocarbons, halocarbons, and inert gases in fire suppression systems;
describe design goals for smoke and fire controls and the corresponding management systems; and
explain fire extinguisher operation, inspection, testing, and maintenance procedures and proper use.
evaluate the financial impact on an organization resulting from an accident;
explain workplace accident legal compliance, including OSHA accident reporting, OSHA recordkeeping regulations, and worker's compensation claims; and
identify and compare accident categories, including near miss, minor injury, major injury, and catastrophic injury.
describe the purpose of corrective actions;
develop an effective corrective action plan for an organization; and
write a report documenting an accident.
explain common unsafe actions such as working at unsafe speeds or using unsafe tools;
describe human, job, and workplace factors that lead to accidents;
explain the importance of timely reporting workplace accidents;
complete a standard accident report form;
write an effective accident report, including a summary of an incident, findings, and recommendations, using factual communication;
identify and report causal factors of an accident; and
analyze accident reports of small damage and near misses and describe future prevention of major accidents.
identify and discuss the purpose and benefits of accident investigations in the workplace;
identify and discuss the role that workers, supervisors, managers, and safety personnel have in the accident investigation process; and
identify and describe the phases of an accident investigation.
ask questions and define problems based on observations or information from text, phenomena, models, or investigations;
apply scientific practices to plan and conduct descriptive, comparative, and experimental investigations and use engineering practices to design solutions to problems;
use appropriate safety equipment and practices during laboratory, classroom, and field investigations as outlined in Texas Education Agency-approved safety standards;
use appropriate tools such as measurement and data collection tools, software, sensors, probes, microscopes, cameras, and glassware;
collect quantitative data using the International System of Units (SI) and qualitative data as evidence;
organize quantitative and qualitative data using notebooks, journals, graphs, charts, tables, spreadsheets, and drawings and models;
develop and use models to represent phenomena, systems, processes, or solutions to engineering problems; and
distinguish between scientific hypotheses, theories, and laws.
identify advantages and limitations of models such as their size, scale, properties, and materials;
analyze data by identifying significant statistical features, patterns, sources of error, and limitations;
use mathematical calculations to assess quantitative relationships in data; and
develop explanations and propose solutions supported by data and models and consistent with scientific ideas, principles, and theories;
communicate explanations and solutions individually and collaboratively in a variety of settings and formats; and
engage respectfully in scientific argumentation using applied scientific explanations and empirical evidence.

analyze, evaluate, and critique scientific explanations and solutions by using empirical evidence, logical reasoning, and experimental and observational testing so as to encourage critical thinking by the student;

relate the impact of past and current research on scientific thought and society, including research methodology, cost-benefit analysis, and contributions of diverse scientists as related to the content; and

research and explore resources such as museums, libraries, professional organizations, private companies, online platforms, and mentors to investigate science, technology, engineering, and mathematics careers.
establish a rationale and preliminary set of ideas for a research question or questions using organizational tools, collaboration, or research;
perform a literature review and evaluate several examples related to the project;
refine a research question by interacting with professionals in the field of study and document the conversations;
distinguish between descriptive, comparative, or experimental research design methodologies;
develop a research question or questions that are testable and measurable;
justify in writing the significance and feasibility of the project;
generate a materials list and propose a cost analysis; and
use the citation style appropriate to the field of study throughout the documentation.
perform background research on the selected investigative problem;
examine hypotheses generated to guide a research process by evaluating the merits and feasibility of the hypotheses; and
identify the control, independent variable, and dependent variables within the research and justify the purpose of each.
write the procedure of the experimental design, including a schematic of the lab, materials, set up, ethical considerations, and safety protocols;
conduct the experiment with the independent and dependent variables;
acquire data using appropriate equipment and technology; and
record observations as they occur within an investigation, including qualitative and quantitative observations such as journals, photographic evidence, logs, tables, and charts.
manipulate data by constructing charts, data tables, or graphs using technology to organize information collected in an experiment;
identify sources of random error and systematic error and differentiate between both types of error;
report error of a set of measured data in various formats such as standard deviation and percent error; and
analyze data using statistical methods to recognize patterns, trends, and proportional relationships.
justify conclusions that are supported by research data;
consider and summarize alternative explanations for observations and results; and
identify limitations within the research process and provide recommendations for additional research.
develop a plan of action on how to present to a target audience;
review artifacts used in the communication of the presentation for errors, grammar, professional standards, and citations;

develop a professional collection or portfolio of work that includes artifacts such as a journal, proposal, written procedures, methodology, iterations, interviews and check ins with professionals, changes within the experiment, and photographic evidence;
practice a professional presentation with peers and educators using a rubric to measure content, skill, and performance;
incorporate feedback provided by a review panel to document for future improvements or changes; and
communicate data analysis and experimental results of original findings of a research project clearly to an audience of professionals.
research and select a problem, issue, or interest within a selected profession or across disciplines for a personal enrichment or career development project;
develop a problem statement, thesis statement, research question, or value proposition statement;
identify and select a design or research process such as engineering design process, design thinking model, scientific discovery, or other industry-standard methodology;
identify and select an appropriate audience for a problem, issue, or interest;
identify key factors such as cost, feasibility, or time constraints necessary for successful development and implementation of a solution or plan; and
identify key resources such as financial, intellectual, physical, human, and digital resources needed for development and implementation of a plan.
research and select appropriate mentor(s) or advisor(s); and
recruit appropriate collaborators, partners, or contributors.
identify and use effective communication strategies to use with mentor(s) or advisor(s) to provide updates and status reports;
research and identify key performance indicators (KPI) that demonstrate successful progress of a project; and
select appropriate method(s) to benchmark measurement of KPI such as a Gantt chart.
define the key activities necessary for successful implementation of a project;
identify deliverable dates for key activities to support completion of a project within an established timeline; and
develop and execute a plan to monitor and complete key deliverables.
identify potential risks such as financial, economic, regulatory, ethical, environmental, or legal risks associated with the design and implementation of the project and the end product; and
evaluate and select methods to mitigate potential risks associated with a project.
research and identify approval processes necessary to implement a project;
prepare and present a proposal for project approval; and
review feedback and revise an original proposal for a project as needed.
complete a project plan that includes problem statement, thesis statement, research question, or value proposition statement; key partners; measurables; deliverables; risk analyses; and approvals;
implement a plan for project completion;
monitor and evaluate the progress of a project plan to determine whether modifications or changes are necessary;
document all phases of a project plan; and
report periodically on the progress of a project plan.
identify an appropriate audience and coordinate the presentation of findings related to a selected problem, issue, or interest;
present findings in a professional manner such as using concise language, engaging content, relevant media, and clear speech;
evaluate feedback received from a presentation;
evaluate the project's potential impact(s) on the identified problem, issue, or interest; and
analyze and report on personal learning experiences such as essential skills gained, areas of personal growth, and challenges encountered throughout the project.
identify different methods to gain employment such as employer websites, job search engines, business locations, networking, and local open forums for job opportunities;
identify and demonstrate essential workplace skills such as eye contact, professional greetings, punctuality, appropriate dress, and effective communication to gain employment;
develop a cover letter and create a resume, curriculum vitae (CV), or portfolio;
demonstrate proper interview techniques in a variety of situations;
create pre-employment documents, including thank you letters, and post-employment documents, including a resignation letter with customary notice provisions;
complete appropriate employment documents, including application, offer letter, I-9 form, and W-4 form; and
describe the benefits of having a job and being self-sufficient.
identify and model appropriate hygiene, grooming, and attire for various workplaces;
demonstrate professionalism by being dependable, working hard, respecting authority, solving problems, taking initiative, communicating effectively, listening actively, and resolving conflicts;
model appropriate workplace etiquette in physical and digital environments;
demonstrate accountability by working with other employees to support the organization, completing assigned tasks and taking responsibility for mistakes; and
demonstrate time management, including prioritizing work to fulfill responsibilities and meeting deadlines.
develop and analyze a personal budget for a variety of economic situations such as part- time and full-time employment;
interpret data from industry-specific tables, charts, and graphs to find solutions to problems;
organize, write, and curate industry-specific documents and electronic communication using appropriate language;
interpret and calculate information included in an earnings statement, including wages, Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) deductions, taxes, and other benefits such as tips earned; and
explain how debt affects financial stability.
explain how interpersonal skills affect human relations on the job;
differentiate between characteristics of successful and non-successful working relationships;
explain the importance of respecting the rights of others;
explain how different personalities, experiences, and workstyles of employees can affect the workplace; and
demonstrate professional verbal and nonverbal communication, including proper phone usage, body language, and interactions with customers and coworkers in person and online.

research and explain workplace policies and procedures related to absence reporting, employee theft, sexual harassment, recognized holidays, workplace safety, acceptable use policy, jury duty, attendance and punctuality, drug-free workplace, and related consequences;
demonstrate responsible behavior by following applicable workplace and school codes of conduct with integrity;
discuss the importance of ethical behavior in the workplace such as treating others with respect, being honest, working to full potential, and developing a quality work product;
summarize the importance of the Fair Labor Standards Act;

describe the potential consequences of violating privacy laws related to Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule (COPPA);

research and explain the origins and legislative intent of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title VII, and the Education Amendments of 1972, Title IX, and the rights and responsibilities established by these laws; and
research and describe laws and regulations related to a student's employment or a chosen industry or career.
identify and demonstrate safe working practices in the workplace;
identify and illustrate solutions related to unsafe work practices;
explain the importance of Occupational Safety and Health Administration regulations in the workplace; and
describe physical health and mental wellness practices that influence job performance.
identify and develop effective leadership skills through participation in activities such as career and technical student organizations;
identify appropriate certifications in the current employment position or desired occupational area;
compare rewards and demands associated with various levels of employment in a variety of careers;
investigate and compare career options by completing interest surveys, career aptitude tests, and skill inventories;
generate short- and long-term Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Realistic, Time-Bound (SMART) goals for personal and career growth;
research and explain methods for developing a growth mindset;
summarize how to appropriately self-advocate in the workplace; and
explain the impact of an employee self-evaluations, management performance evaluations, and employee feedback responses on personal job growth.
evaluate and compare career options, including salaries and benefits;
describe how interests, abilities, personal priorities, and family responsibilities affect career choices;
identify continuing education opportunities that enhance career advancement and promote lifelong learning;
analyze the future employment outlook in an occupational area of interest;
describe entrepreneurial opportunities in an occupational area of interest; and
evaluate strategies for career retention and advancement in response to the changing global workforce.
differentiate between a job and a career;
refine an industry-specific professional portfolio or resume;
identify appropriate sources for writing and obtain letters of recommendation;
model proper interview skills based on a chosen career cluster;
evaluate the effectiveness of various methods to gain employment;
describe how having a job can lead to a career and self-sufficiency; and
identify and explain work-based benefits such as health insurance, direct deposit, and retirement contributions.
maintain appropriate hygiene, grooming, and attire for the workplace;
model appropriate workplace etiquette in physical and digital environments;
justify time-management decisions to fulfill responsibilities and meet deadlines;
analyze employer expectations by reflecting on evaluations;
demonstrate effective listening skills used in the workplace through appropriate interactions with customers and coworkers; and
cultivate and improve professionalism by continuously being dependable, working hard, respecting authority, solving problems, taking initiative, communicating effectively, and listening actively.
integrate mathematical concepts into business transactions such as counting inventory, calculating discounts, and conducting cash transactions;
compare earning potential for careers within a selected program of study with personal financial goals;
analyze and apply data from industry-specific tables, charts, or graphs to generate solutions to problems; and
analyze and synthesize information from electronic communications, including forms, reports, or summaries.
identify positive interpersonal skills, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and respect for all people, and model these skills as a mentor with peers;
apply effective verbal, nonverbal, written, or electronic communication skills to a variety of audiences;
define personal integrity and evaluate its effects on human relations in the workplace;
classify a variety of working relationships into functional and dysfunctional characteristics; and
participate in leadership and career-development activities related to a selected program of study.
evaluate provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act;

analyze the legal consequences of violating privacy laws related to Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA);
research and describe laws governing different professions within a selected program of study;
analyze organizational policies and procedures and ethical standards from the student's current place of employment; and
interpret and evaluate the rights and responsibilities of employers and employees.
research and describe different types of identity theft to identify associated risks and prevention strategies;
identify and evaluate consequences of breach of personal and occupational safety practices in the workplace;
model safe working practices at a training station;
evaluate the impact of Occupational Safety and Health Administration regulations in the workplace; and
analyze how physical health and mental wellness practices influence career longevity and satisfaction in a career within a selected program of study.

create a personal growth plan that identifies relevant certifications, postsecondary opportunities, and technical skills required for various levels of employment based on a chosen career within a selected program of study and describe how to obtain them;
develop short- and long-term Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Realistic, Time-Bound (SMART) goals based on personal and professional growth plans;
analyze the rewards and demands of career advancement;
model appropriate self-advocacy in various workplace scenarios;
compare current employee performance evaluations to previous evaluations to identify areas of growth and opportunities for continued development; and
evaluate and compare employment advancement considerations such as salaries, benefits, and qualifications.
research and compare declining and growth industries across career clusters;
identify and analyze future job growth within a selected program of study based on societal needs;
analyze the skills required to be successful in emerging industries;
identify continuing education opportunities to determine education and training requirements for future careers within a selected program of study;
research and evaluate entrepreneurial opportunities related to a selected program of study; and
evaluate how personal priorities such as interests, abilities, and family responsibilities may influence career choice.
identify and participate in training, education, or preparation for licensure, certification, or other relevant credentials to prepare for employment;
complete work tasks with high standards to ensure delivery of quality products and services; and
demonstrate and apply planning and time-management skills to work tasks.
demonstrate and apply professional standards and personal qualities needed to be employable such as punctuality, initiative, patience, kindness, respect for authority, and cooperation;
apply appropriate content knowledge, technical concepts, and vocabulary in the workplace;
apply effective listening skills to obtain and clarify information in the workplace; and
maintain appropriate hygiene, grooming, and attire in the workplace.
employ critical-thinking skills to solve problems and make decisions; and
analyze elements of a problem to develop creative and innovative solutions.
demonstrate teamwork using conflict-management skills to achieve collective goals;
apply verbal and non-verbal communication skills consistently in a manner that is clear, concise, and effective; and
model effective internal and external communications to support work activities.
demonstrate a positive work ethic by performing assigned tasks as directed;
model ethical reasoning in workplace situations;
comply with all applicable rules, laws, and regulations in the workplace; and
research and explain the roles of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) and the Texas Workforce Commission (TWC) in the workplace.
follow workplace safety rules and regulations consistently;
operate tools and equipment used in the workplace safely;
report and handle accidents and safety incidents according to workplace procedures as necessary; and
describe and perform a hazard analysis of the workplace.
conduct, document, and evaluate learning activities in a supervised employment experience;
assess and report on advanced technical knowledge and skills related to the student's occupational objective and growth;
evaluate strengths and weaknesses in technical skill proficiency; and
document experiences related to the workplace and curate work samples.
